intro: Interior clarity. A considered finish. Detailing designed around your vehicle and the way you drive.
serviceIntro: Start with the condition of your vehicle, then select the treatment that makes sense. Illustrative package prices are starting points.

offers.title: The refresh
offers.text: A careful reset for a vehicle in regularly maintained condition.

offers.title: The interior reset
offers.text: Time and attention for the cabin you spend your day in.

offers.title: The complete detail
offers.text: A fuller interior and exterior treatment, scoped to the vehicle.

story.title: The small details change the whole drive.
story.text: Leather, fabric, trim, and paint have different needs. A useful treatment begins with the vehicle’s actual condition and a clear explanation of what can improve.

guide.title: A finish worth understanding.
guide.intro: Good detailing sets clear expectations for the result and the care that follows.

notes.title: Condition comes first
notes.text: Pet hair, sand, spills, and embedded stains change the time and methods needed. Share those details before choosing a package.

notes.title: Know what protection means
notes.text: Wax, sealant, and coating services are different. A real provider should explain preparation, durability assumptions, and aftercare for the selected product.

notes.title: Plan the mobile setup
notes.text: A safe working area, access, weather, and utilities can affect mobile service. The appointment request should confirm requirements before the visit.

notes.title: Keep the result in perspective
notes.text: Deep damage, permanent staining, and clear-coat defects may need specialist work. The site should never promise that every mark will disappear.

faq.q: Do these prices include every vehicle?
faq.a: No. They are illustrative starting prices for the demo. Vehicle size, condition, service depth, and access would inform a real quote.
Not always. This example promises no restoration result. A real assessment should explain limitations before work begins.

faq.q: Are the photos of mobile customer visits?
faq.a: No. The stock images show detailing craft in a workshop. They do not document the fictional business’s work or mobile setup.
